messages:
marta (support): Heads-up — acme_inc just opened an escalated ticket: intermittent 502/504s from the hosted API edge during streaming/long-poll embeddings. They say spikes started after they toggled client streaming to seq-chunks. Ticket ID #ACM-412.
liam (oncall): Can you drop the earliest trace ids and a short repro? Is this only for embeddings or generation too?
marta (support): Only embeddings so far, large batch stream (~150 req/min), chunk_size=256. Customer shared two trace ids: trace/0a1b2c3d and trace/4f5e6d7c. Also attached a short curl repro they used.
customer:acme_inc: repro (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/stream \
  -d '{"model":"open-v1","input_chunk_size":256,"items":[...150 items...]}'
```
marta (support): Their client shows initial handshake ok, then a series of RST_STREAM / 502s within 200-600ms of stream start. They included one edge-side snippet: 
```
[envoy] upstream reset: connection error: connection reset by peer, downstream request id=0a1b2c3d
[nginx] 502 while reading response header from upstream
```
liam (oncall): Thx. @sam can you check ingress h2 connpool metrics for the us-east region around 10:22 UTC? Look for keepalive count and active stream limit per connection. Suspect h2 window/stream exhaustion.
sam (eng-sre): Pulling metrics now. I see a sharp drop in healthy upstream connections at 10:21:42 and a concurrent spike in CONNECT_RESET downstream. Active streams per connection hit ~98 (limit configured 100) right before resets. Also see 504s for requests queued > 30s.
emily (eng-runtime): Are these clients reusing connections? If client opens many short-lived h2 conns that could exhaust the upstream pool. Any auth header size differences?
marta (support): customer says they switched language client lib to keepalive=true, but tested with default limiter off. They also noted request header added: X-ACME-TRACE-ID which is long (~900 chars).
liam (oncall): That long header could force HTTP/2 HEADERS frame fragmentation and push memory/counters up. But the stream count hitting 98/100 is more suspicious. Two-pronged: 1) pool exhaustion due to high stream concurrency per conn, 2) header bloat slowing header processing.
sam (eng-sre): Reproduced a small load locally with header length ~900 and concurrent streams ~120 across few connections — upstream side started resetting streams and envoy returned 502. Looks consistent.
emily (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation: increase per-connection max concurrent streams on upstream proxy (nginx/envoy) from 100 -> 200 and bump ingress upstream connection pool in us-east by 25% to absorb burst. Longer term: add client header length guard and better queue/backpressure on embeddings path.
liam (oncall): Can we push a small config roll (canary) on ingress for us-east now? Deploy-bot: rollout request queued.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: ingress-config/us-east-canary by liam at 4794012365.
sam (eng-sre): Canary shows successful handshake with acme repro: no 502s after bump; active streams per connection now ~60, pool healthy.
marta (support): I informed customer and asked them to re-run their repro. They re-ran and reported: 
"looks good for the last 10 minutes, previous 502s disappeared but we'll monitor." :thumbsup:
liam (oncall): Action items:
- sam: monitor us-east ingress for 24h, capture any RST_STREAMs and trace ids.
- emily: follow up with runtime team to add header-length telemetry and a conservative reject path.
- marta: keep ACME ticket open and coordinate customer retest; escalate if they see recurrence.
- sam/liam: schedule a config review to decide permanent stream/pool limits.
marta (support): noted. I'll attach the env logs, trace ids, and the temporary config diff to the ticket. Closing loop here once customer confirms 24h stability.
customer:acme_inc: thanks team — appreciate the fast canary and updates. We'll shout if it reappears.
liam (oncall): Nice triage everyone. Marking postmortem not required unless it recurs. :eyes:
